tldr:
For the exact overlap-population causal effect, Theorem private-overlap-frontier determines the pure-central-private minimax MSE and finite-sample honest connected-interval length in the known one-covariate uniform-design experiment. The class requires binary treatment and outcome, \(1/5\le e\le4/5\), and Hölder marginal regressions \(e,m\); individual outcome cells may be zero and \(k\) is otherwise measurable. Uniformly over \(n\ge2\) and \(0<\varepsilon\le1\), MSE is of order \(\rho_s^2\) and maximal expected honest length is of order \(\rho_s\), where
\[
 \rho_s=\min\{1,\max[n^{-1/2},n^{-4s/(4s+1)},(n\varepsilon)^{-1},(n^2\varepsilon)^{-2s/(2s+1)}]\}.
\]
An explicit occupancy-normalized covariance/variance release attains both orders with full-record privacy on every dataset. Legal deterministic-target priors and a Borel fixed-sample coupling give the matching all-mechanism converse. No essential logarithm occurs, and consistency holds exactly when \(n\varepsilon_n\to\infty\). This is a specialized ATO benchmark for confidential analyses, including the estimand supported by WeightIt.
gap: The closest repository sibling concerns point-CATE; this target is a global overlap ratio containing quadratic integral functionals. The proposed deterministic-target lower mixture separates that global ratio and targets a different smoothness/privacy phase diagram. Ohnishi and Awan supply smooth private ATO methodology, including point-estimator consistency and an MSE order in Theorem 3.2 and variance-estimator privacy and consistency in Theorem 3.3. Those results do not determine the rough \(e,m\)-only, pure-private, finite-sample matched point-risk and honest connected-interval frontier.
fill: The release and coupling handles test the explicit conjectural target \(\rho_s^{\mathrm{cand}}\), including its no-consistency truncation, against the same full-class point-risk and honest-length criteria. Exact projected moments, sensitivity on arbitrary datasets and finite-sample mixture bookkeeping are proof obligations. WeightIt ATO users receive a sample-size and privacy-budget benchmark for this one-covariate class.
